questions.question: What does Franek say about the plane when the bomber appears on television?
answers: That he flew it yesterday
That his plane was burning and that it was a Corsair
That he saw it in a museum
That it was grandpa's plane
questions.explanation: Franek says calmly: "My plane was burning – it was a Corsair. I didn't make it back to the carrier."

questions.question: Which pilot's name does Anna first find in the military archives?
answers: Jack Larsen
Daniel Rakowiecki
Michał Kosakowski
Piotr Wójcik
questions.explanation: On the list of pilots who fell at the Battle of Iwo Jima appears Daniel Rakowiecki from Detroit.

questions.question: What explanation does Doctor Kosakowski propose?
answers: That Franek was certainly a pilot in a past life
That the brain assembled scraps of information into a coherent story — cryptomnesia and memory reconstruction
That Franek is pretending out of boredom
That it's an effect of hypnosis at nursery school
questions.explanation: Kosakowski explains cryptomnesia: the mind forgets the source of the information but assembles it into one narrative.

questions.question: What does Kosakowski call confirmation bias?
answers: Forgetting the names of loved ones
Selectively collecting evidence for a story we already believe
A false memory after hypnosis
An error in the military archives
questions.explanation: When something seems true, we begin collecting only the evidence "for" and ignore the contradictions.

questions.question: What does Anna whisper to Franek at the end?
answers: That he must forget about the plane
Whoever you were — now you are mine
That tomorrow they are going to the museum
That his father was also a pilot
questions.explanation: Anna kisses her son and says: "Whoever you were – now you are mine."
